comments.body:
THIRD instance tonight, and it reveals a facet the original report missed.

## New fact: the 8,000-char cap is ALSO a completion criterion, not only a plan-review admission limit

Ticket `337e-b558-17a2-49bd`'s close was refused by the COMPLETION VERIFIER, with exactly one
failing criterion, read from its `completion_verifier_fail_v1` sidecar:

    verdict:   FAIL
    findings:  1
    criterion: "ticket description is at most 8,000 characters"

Its description was **8,320** characters. Nothing about the implementation was in question — the
change (Gerrit 2652) was merged, both gates green, all acceptance criteria ticked and evidenced.
The ticket simply could not be closed because its description was 320 characters too long.

So the cap bites in TWO independent places:

1. **`review-plan` admission** — an over-cap description is refused, which is what the original
   report covered.
2. **`verify-completion`** — an over-cap description is a FAILING completion criterion, so the
   ticket cannot close at all.

(2) is the more consequential one and was not in the original report. It means an over-cap ticket
is not merely awkward to revise: it is **unclosable** until someone shortens it, regardless of
whether the work is done.

## Why the composition is worse than either half

Shortening the description is a TEXT change, which invalidates the plan-review attestation
(`stale-material`). So closing an over-cap ticket requires: trim -> re-run `review-plan` (a
15-20 minute billable gate) -> close (a further ~10 minutes). For a ticket whose code merged hours
ago and whose criteria are already met.

## The three instances tonight

| ticket | chars | how it surfaced |
|---|---|---|
| `9183-aaae` (S2) | 7,994 -> 8,088 | correcting a factually wrong AC pushed it over; the re-review the close then demanded would itself have refused admission |
| `bff5-9163` | 11,782 | widening `file_impact` to match the merged commit forced a re-review the description could not be admitted for |
| `337e-b558` | 8,320 | completion verifier FAILED the close on the cap alone |

Each was resolved the same way — relocating evidence prose into ticket comments until the
description fit. That works, and arguably improves the tickets (evidence belongs in comments,
plan belongs in the description). But it is a workaround discovered three times independently,
and the pressure it applies is toward deleting the explanation of a correction at exactly the
moment a correction is being made.

## Additional acceptance criterion this implies

- [ ] The completion verifier's enforcement of the description cap is settled deliberately: either
      an over-cap description should NOT block a close whose criteria are otherwise met (the cap
      exists to bound REVIEW cost, and a close is not a review), or if it should, the refusal must
      name the remedy and the fact that trimming will force a re-review — so the operator learns
      the full cost up front rather than after a 15-minute gate.

compiled_state.description:
## The trap

Correcting an acceptance criterion on an already-reviewed ticket can make the ticket
**unclosable without a prose rewrite**, because two independent mechanisms compose badly:

1. Editing description TEXT invalidates the plan-review attestation (`stale-material`), so the
   close gate refuses and demands a fresh `review-plan`.
2. `review-plan` refuses admission for a description above `verify.max_ticket_description_chars`
   (8,000).

So if the description is already near the cap, ANY correction that adds characters pushes it over,
and the re-review that the close now requires becomes inadmissible.

## Observed, 2026-09-05, on `9183-aaae-667d-45e6` (S2 of epic 6202)

The ticket's AC4 read "A validated `daemon.json` change on a live daemon reloads Docker, never
restarts." That specifies behaviour that cannot work — dockerd's SIGHUP reload does not apply
`builder.gc`, which the implementation documents and deliberately refuses. Correcting the AC to
match reality took the description from **7,994 to 8,088 chars**, six characters of headroom
consumed and 88 over.

Result: `rebar transition ... closed` refused with `stale-material`, and the prescribed remedy
("Run `rebar review-plan` separately, then retry close") would itself have refused on admission.
Recovered by compressing the correction to 90 characters and relying on a ticket comment to carry
the reasoning — total 7,998.

## Why this is worth recording rather than shrugging at

Descriptions cluster just under the cap, because authors write until the limit stops them. That
makes "already near the cap" the COMMON case, not an edge case, so the trap is reachable by any
agent that later finds a factually wrong AC. The pressure it applies is in the wrong direction:
it makes deleting the explanation of a correction the cheapest way out, exactly when a correction
is the thing most worth explaining.

Both mechanisms are individually correct and should be kept. `stale-material` is right — the plan
did change. The admission cap is right — it bounds review cost. Only their composition is hostile.

## Not yet root-caused; possible directions, none endorsed

- Exempt the Acceptance Criteria block from the admission character count (it is the part a
  reviewer most needs and the part corrections land in).
- Let the close gate's `stale-material` refusal distinguish a correction that only REMOVES or
  REWORDS a criterion from one that adds scope, as it already distinguishes checkbox ticks (which
  are correctly normalised out of the fingerprint).
- Report remaining headroom in the `rebar edit` success line, not only when the cap is breached,
  so the trap is visible before it closes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The interaction is root-caused: confirm both mechanisms fire as described, and establish
      how many current tickets sit within (say) 200 chars of the cap, to size the exposure.
- [ ] Correcting a wrong AC on a reviewed, near-cap ticket no longer requires deleting prose to
      stay admissible — by whichever of the directions above survives review.
- [ ] A regression test drives the composed path end to end: reviewed ticket at cap-minus-epsilon
      -> AC text correction -> close, and asserts it does not deadlock on admission.
- [ ] Whatever changes, `stale-material` still fires on a genuine plan change and the admission
      cap still bounds review cost — neither guard is weakened to buy the ergonomics.
